AD.name: Andorra
AD.notes: Impost General Indirecte (Llei 11/2012). 1% food, water, books, newspapers/magazines; 2.5% passenger transport and cultural services (museums, cinemas, concerts); 9.5% increased rate on banking/financial services; 0% public health, education, housing rental.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.notes: 0% on healthcare, education, international transport, first supply of residential property, exports. Domestic passenger transport, bare land, some financial services exempt. Food is standard-rated (5%).

AF.name: Afghanistan
AF.notes: No functioning VAT (a 10% VAT law was enacted in 2020 but not implemented). Business receipts tax (BRT) on gross receipts: 4% general, 2% restaurants, higher (up to 10%) for telecoms/airlines/large hotels. Low confidence: rates under current authorities not verified from official source.

AG.name: Antigua and Barbuda
AG.notes: Antigua and Barbuda Sales Tax 17% from 1 Jan 2024 (was 15%); 14% hotel/reduced rate abolished (hotel accommodation now 17%).

AI.name: Anguilla
AI.notes: 13% standard (since 1 Jul 2022), zero-rated items. Regime restructured with an Import Goods Tax effective 1 Aug 2025; rate on services stays 13%.

AL.name: Albania
AL.notes: Local: TVSH. 6% accommodation, agritourism, books, audiovisual advertising. 10% agricultural inputs. Basic food at 20%. Draft 2027 package (21% standard, 6% food, 10% tourism) NOT enacted.

AM.name: Armenia
AM.notes: Local: AAH. Single 20% rate; exports zero-rated; most financial and education services exempt. SMEs often on turnover tax instead of VAT.

AO.name: Angola
AO.notes: 5% on basic-basket foods and agricultural inputs (VAT Code Tables I/II); 7% hotel and restaurant services (conditions apply); 1%/2% only in Cabinda province.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.notes: 21% general. 27% on utilities (telecom, gas, water, sewerage, electricity) supplied to non-dwelling (business) premises; households pay 21%. 10.5% on certain items: housing construction, passenger transport <=100 km, some medical assistance, live cattle, certain capital goods, consumer loan interest. Exempt (no IVA): books, ordinary natural water, common bread, milk, medicine (per PwC), stamps. 27% is an increased rate, so it is not listed in 'reduced'.

AT.name: Austria
AT.notes: Listed staple foods 4.9% from 1 Jul 2026 (Annex 3 UStG); most other food 10%. Feminine hygiene products and contraceptives 0% from 1 Jan 2026. Jungholz and Mittelberg use 19% (German-customs enclaves).

AU.name: Australia
AU.notes: 10% GST. GST-free (zero-rated): most basic food (not restaurant/takeaway/hot food, confectionery, soft drinks), most health and medical supplies incl. prescription medicines, education, water and sewerage, exports. Input-taxed: residential rent, financial supplies. Applies on Norfolk Island since 2016.

AW.name: Aruba
AW.notes: No VAT; cumulative turnover taxes total 7% (BBO + BAVP + BAZV) since 2023, normally passed on to consumers; component split reported differently by sources. Planned 12.5% VAT postponed indefinitely.

AZ.name: Azerbaijan
AZ.notes: Local: ƏDV. Single 18% rate; exports and international transport zero-rated.

BA.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
BA.notes: Local: PDV. Single 17% rate, no reduced rates; exports zero-rated; some exemptions.

BB.name: Barbados
BB.notes: 17.5% standard; 10% on hotel accommodation/tourism; some basic items zero-rated.

BD.name: Bangladesh
BD.notes: VAT and Supplementary Duty Act 2012 (in force 1 Jul 2019). Standard 15%; reduced/truncated rates 1.5-10% for listed goods/services (Second Schedule); First Schedule items exempt (unprocessed food staples, medical services etc.); exports zero-rated. Supplementary duty 10-500% on some goods. Restaurants 5% (catering 15%). FY2025-26 budget raised e.g. flats VAT 7.5%->10% and online sales commission 5%->15%.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.notes: Hotels/campsites 6%->12% from 1 Mar 2026 (planned takeaway-meal rise withdrawn; takeaway food stays 6%). Restaurant 12% excludes drinks (21%). Daily/weekly newspapers 0% under conditions, other periodicals 6%. Residential electricity 6%.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.notes: 9% only for hotel accommodation, books (print and electronic), baby food and baby nappies. Restaurant 9% and bread/flour 0% ended 1 Jan 2025. Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 Jan 2026.

BH.name: Bahrain
BH.notes: Raised from 5% on 1 Jan 2022. 0% on 118 listed basic food items (NBR list, Sept 2024), qualifying medicines/medical services, basic education, local transport, new residential construction, exports. Non-listed food is 10%.

BI.name: Burundi
BI.notes: 18% standard; 10% intermediate rate on certain goods (sugar at 10% from 2026/27 Finance Law).

BL.name: Saint Barthélemy
BL.notes: French VAT does not apply; local taxes only.

BM.name: Bermuda
BM.notes: No VAT or general sales tax; customs duty on imports (PwC: VAT NA).

BN.name: Brunei
BN.notes: No VAT, GST or sales tax.

BO.name: Bolivia
BO.notes: 13% included in the price (tax-inclusive; ~14.94% on a net basis). No reduced rates; exports zero-rated.

BQ.name: Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba)
BQ.notes: Bonaire ABB: 8% goods/imports, 6% services, 7% insurance. Sint Eustatius and Saba: 6% goods, 4% services, 5% insurance. Values from aggregator; check Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.notes: Brazil has no single national VAT rate. 'standard' 20 = the most common state modal (internal) ICMS rate in 2026 (8 of 27 UFs); São Paulo is 18%, range 17% (ES, MS, MT, RS, SC) to 23% (MA). Use 'regions' for the buyer's state. 'reduced' 4/7/12 are interstate ICMS rates (B2B), not consumer rates; states also apply reduced rates to the cesta básica (e.g. 7-12%) and higher rates (25-30%+) on alcohol, tobacco, arms, jewellery. Other taxes on top: federal PIS/COFINS 3.65% (cumulative) or 9.25% (non-cumulative); IPI 0-30%+ on manufactured goods; municipal ISS 2-5% on services (services generally bear ISS, not ICMS). Tax reform: 2026 is the CBS/IBS test year - 0.9% CBS + 0.1% IBS shown on invoices, offset against PIS/COFINS and waived for taxpayers meeting ancillary obligations (net cost ~0; Simples Nacional not required). CBS replaces PIS/COFINS from 2027; IBS phases in 2029-2032 while ICMS/ISS phase out by 2033. ICMS is charged 'por dentro' (included in its own base).

AL.name: Alagoas
AL.note: 19% until 31 Mar 2026; poverty-fund surcharge on specific products only

SE.name: Sergipe
SE.note: 1% poverty-fund surcharge on specific products only

BS.name: Bahamas
BS.notes: 10% standard (since 1 Jan 2022). Unprepared grocery food: 10%->5% (Apr 2025) then VAT-free from 1 Apr 2026 (described by government as exempt); prepared/restaurant food 10%. 5% reduced rate on selected essentials (e.g. some medical/hygiene items).

BT.name: Bhutan
BT.notes: GST at 5% from 1 Jan 2026 (GST Act 2020 as amended 2025; rate cut from proposed 7%), replacing sales tax and parts of excise. Small exempt list (basic food items), exports zero-rated. Registration threshold BTN 5 million.

BW.name: Botswana
BW.notes: 14%; VAT Act 2026 (1 Jul 2026) narrowed zero-rating: revised zero-rated foods (maize/sorghum meal, brown bread, rice, sugar, cooking oil, some fresh produce); milk now 14%; prescription medicines zero-rated; VAT on private medical services suspended.

BY.name: Belarus
BY.notes: Local: NDS. 10% on listed foodstuffs and children's goods (and some agricultural products). Telecom services at a higher rate (25%/26% reported; unverified).

BZ.name: Belize
BZ.notes: General Sales Tax 12.5%; some basic foods, medicines zero-rated/exempt.

CA.name: Canada
CA.notes: Federal GST 5%. HST provinces (NB, NL, NS, ON, PE) charge a single HST that includes the 5% GST (gst field 0 there). QC adds QST 9.975%; BC PST 7%; MB RST 7%; SK PST 6% (PSTs are not charged on GST). AB, NT, NU, YT: GST only. Zero-rated: basic groceries, prescription drugs, qualifying medical devices, feminine hygiene products, exports. Restaurant meals and snacks are taxable. Nova Scotia HST 15->14% from 1 Apr 2025. Temporary GST/HST break 14 Dec 2024-15 Feb 2025 on certain items (ended). Provincial point-of-sale rebates (e.g. books, children's clothing in some HST provinces) not modelled.

CD.name: DR Congo
CD.notes: 16%; 1% on specific essential goods (certain foods, agricultural inputs); 5% domestic air tickets; 0% exports.

CF.name: Central African Republic
CF.notes: 19% standard; reported 5% reduced rate not verified.

CG.name: Congo
CG.notes: 18% VAT + 5% surtax on the VAT amount = 18.9%. 5% reduced rate on listed products.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.notes: Local: MWST/TVA/IVA. 2.6% foodstuffs (non-alcoholic), medicines, printed and electronic books/newspapers without advertising, water in pipes, menstrual products (from 1 Jan 2025). 3.8% special rate for accommodation incl. breakfast. Restaurant service 8.1%. Cultural events, hospital treatment exempt without credit. Same rates apply in Liechtenstein (customs/VAT union) and the German enclave Büsingen.

CI.name: Côte d'Ivoire
CI.notes: 18%; 9% on milk, infant milk/food, luxury rice, non-ECOWAS meat, durum pasta.

CK.name: Cook Islands
CK.notes: VAT 15% on most goods and services.

CL.name: Chile
CL.notes: Single 19% rate on goods and most services; no reduced rates. Exports zero-rated. Digital services 19% since June 2020; Law 21,713 extended VAT to low-value imported goods via platforms (removed USD 41 import exemption).

CM.name: Cameroon
CM.notes: 19.25% = 17.5% VAT + 10% additional council surcharge. 2026 Finance Law: 10% reduced rate for social-housing transactions. Exports 0%.

CN.name: China
CN.notes: VAT Law in force 1 Jan 2026 (with Implementing Regulations) kept the 13% / 9% / 6% structure. 13% goods; 9% necessities (agricultural products/grain, edible oil, tap water, gas, heating, books, newspapers, magazines) and transport, postal, basic telecoms, construction, real estate; 6% most other services (catering, accommodation, cultural/sports, financial, modern services). Small-scale taxpayers 3% (reduced to 1% until 31 Dec 2027). Exports 0%.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.notes: 19% general; 5% on listed goods (some grains, vegetable oils, animal feed, agricultural equipment, electric/hybrid vehicles); 0% exempt-with-credit (meat, fresh eggs, dairy, exports, low/mid-income residential internet). Excluded (no IVA): public passenger transport by land/water, public utilities, many basic foods and medicines. Restaurants and bars generally charge the 8% national consumption tax (impuesto nacional al consumo) instead of IVA.

CR.name: Costa Rica
CR.notes: 13% general; reduced 4% (e.g. domestic air tickets, private health services), 2% (medicines, private education, personal insurance), 1% (canasta básica basic basket).

CU.name: Cuba
CU.notes: Sales/services tax 10% for taxpayers in the statutory scope (not a broad VAT).

CV.name: Cabo Verde
CV.notes: 15% standard; 8% on electricity and water to private consumers.

CW.name: Curaçao
CW.notes: Turnover tax (OB) 6% general; 7% on short-term tourist lodging/rental and insurance; 9% on certain luxury goods (not confirmed for 2026). Currency: Caribbean guilder (XCG) since 31 Mar 2025.

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.notes: 0% on baby milk/nappies, women hygiene products and fresh fruit/vegetables until 31 Dec 2026. City/rural buses 5%, taxis and intercity buses 9%. Northern Cyprus not covered.

CZ.name: Czechia
CZ.notes: Since 1 Jan 2024 the 10% and 15% rates merged into one 12% rate; books 0%. Drinks served in restaurants (other than water and selected drinks) 21%.

DE.name: Germany
DE.notes: Restaurant/catering food permanently 7% from 1 Jan 2026 (Steueränderungsgesetz 2025, Bundesrat 19 Dec 2025); drinks in restaurants stay 19%. Medicines 19%. Local public transport (<=50 km) and rail 7%. Short-term accommodation 7% (breakfast etc 19%). Small PV installations 0%. Heligoland and Büsingen outside the VAT area.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.notes: Single 25% rate. Newspapers published at least monthly 0% (print and electronic). Passenger transport (buses, trains, taxis) VAT-exempt. Many cultural activities exempt. Zero VAT on books proposed (bill L 36, from 1 Jul 2027) - not law. Faroe Islands and Greenland are outside Danish VAT.

DM.name: Dominica
DM.notes: 15% standard; 10% on accommodation and dive services.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.notes: ITBIS 18%; 16% on specified items (e.g. some dairy, coffee, sugars, cocoa, edible oils). Restaurants also add 10% service charge (not a tax).

DZ.name: Algeria
DZ.notes: 19% standard, 9% reduced (basic goods, some medicines, transport). Tourism/hotel services 9% temporarily until 31 Dec 2027 (from Jan 2025). 2026 Finance Law extended 9% to bus passenger transport, some health services, training, housing rehabilitation.

EC.name: Ecuador
EC.notes: 15% since 1 Apr 2024 (was 12%; Ley Orgánica para Enfrentar el Conflicto Armado Interno). 0%: basic foods, medicines, public transport, electricity and other listed items. 5% on construction materials (since 2024). Government may temporarily cut to 8% for tourism services on holidays.

EE.name: Estonia
EE.notes: Standard 20%->22% (1 Jan 2024) ->24% (1 Jul 2025). Accommodation 9%->13% and press publications 5%->9% from 1 Jan 2025.

EG.name: Egypt
EG.notes: 14% since 1 Jul 2017. 5% on machinery/equipment for production lines. Schedule (table) tax on listed goods/services. Law 157/2025 (18 Jul 2025) moved construction/contracting (5% table tax) and news agency services (exempt) to 14%. Exports 0%.

ES.name: Spain
ES.notes: Basic foods (bread, milk, cheese, eggs, fruit, vegetables, legumes, cereals, olive oil) 4%; other food 10%; sugary soft drinks 21%. Medicines for human use 4%. Electricity/gas temporarily 10% from 22 Mar to 31 May 2026 (RDL 7/2026), back to 21%; further cuts are conditional on electricity CPI. Canary Islands use IGIC (7% general) instead of VAT; Ceuta and Melilla use IPSI.

ET.name: Ethiopia
ET.notes: 15% unchanged under VAT Proclamation 1341/2024 (from July 2024); zero-rated exports and international transport; 15% on non-resident digital services.

FI.name: Finland
FI.notes: Standard 24%->25.5% on 1 Sep 2024. On 1 Jan 2025 books, medicines, passenger transport, accommodation and culture moved 10%->14%; on 1 Jan 2026 the 14% rate fell to 13.5% (food, restaurants etc.). Newspapers/periodicals 10%. Tap water at standard rate. Åland is outside the EU VAT area but uses the same rates.

FJ.name: Fiji
FJ.notes: VAT cut 15%->12.5% from 1 Aug 2025 (2025-26 Budget); kept at 12.5% in 2026-27 Budget. Zero-rated: 21-22 essential food/household items and prescribed medicines. A separate 5% tourism services tax applies from 1 Sep 2026 (plus existing STT/ECAL on hotels).

FM.name: Micronesia
FM.notes: No national VAT/GST (national gross revenue tax on businesses). Individual states levy sales taxes (around 5%, varies by state).

FO.name: Faroe Islands
FO.notes: Local: MVG (meirvirðisgjald). 25% standard; reduced/zero categories for consumers not verified.

FR.name: France
FR.notes: Reimbursable medicines 2.1%, non-reimbursed 10%. Shows/cinema/concerts 5.5%, exhibitions/sites 10%. Restaurant 10% (alcohol 20%). The 5.5% rate on electricity/gas subscription charges was removed 1 Aug 2025 (now 20%). Corsica has special rates; Guadeloupe, Martinique, Réunion 8.5%/2.1%; French Guiana and Mayotte: VAT not applied.

GA.name: Gabon
GA.notes: 18%; 10% and 5% on specific listed products; 0% exports.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.notes: Food zero-rated except catering, hot takeaway, confectionery, crisps, soft drinks, alcohol. Prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacist 0%; over-the-counter medicines 20% (value shown). Domestic fuel/power 5%. Admission by public bodies/eligible cultural bodies exempt; other events 20%. Private school fees 20% from 1 Jan 2025. Temporary 5% on in-scope children's meals, children's tickets and family attractions ran 25 Jun - 1 Sep 2026 (ended). Domestic electricity in Great Britain temporarily 0% from 1 Oct 2026 to 31 Mar 2027 (R&C Brief 10 (2026), SI 2026/987); Northern Ireland stays 5%; domestic gas and other fuel stay 5%.

Northern Ireland.note: EU VAT rules for goods; domestic electricity 5% (GB 0% until 31 Mar 2027)

GD.name: Grenada
GD.notes: 15% standard; 10% on accommodation and qualifying dive services.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.notes: Local: dghg. Single 18% rate; exports zero-rated; various exemptions.

GF.name: French Guiana
GF.notes: VAT (TVA) provisionally not applied in French Guiana; dock dues (octroi de mer) apply instead.

GG.name: Guernsey
GG.notes: No VAT/GST. GST proposal for 2028 in the 2025 Budget, under debate as of Aug 2026.

GH.name: Ghana
GH.notes: Effective 20% = VAT 15% + NHIL 2.5% + GETFund levy 2.5%, all on the same base and creditable since 1 Jan 2026 (VAT Act 2025, Act 1151). 1% COVID-19 levy abolished; flat-rate scheme abolished (previous effective rate ~21.9%). Unprocessed food, medical/pharmaceutical products, education generally exempt.

GI.name: Gibraltar
GI.notes: No VAT. New Transaction Tax on GOODS only (not services) under the UK-EU Gibraltar treaty, provisionally applied from 15 Jul 2026 (replacing import duty): 15% year 1, 16% year 2, 17% from year 3. Treaty allows reduced (>=5%) and 0% rates for essentials (food, water, medicines, books, newspapers, children's clothing); actual lists not confirmed.

GL.name: Greenland
GL.notes: No VAT; import duties on some goods.

GM.name: Gambia
GM.notes: 15% standard (weakly sourced; official GRA page not checked).

GP.name: Guadeloupe
GP.notes: French overseas department: 8.5% normal rate, 2.1% reduced rate (mainland French rates do not apply).

GQ.name: Equatorial Guinea
GQ.notes: 15%; 5% on limited list of basic consumables and books; 0% on certain medical products and equipment.

GR.name: Greece
GR.notes: TEDB code EL. Some basic foods 6%; theatre/concert/cinema tickets 6%, zoos etc. 13%. Islands of Leros, Lesvos, Kos, Samos and Chios: rates reduced by 30% (17/9/4).

GT.name: Guatemala
GT.notes: 12% single rate (included in price). Small taxpayers may use a 5% simplified regime on gross income (not a VAT rate).

GW.name: Guinea-Bissau
GW.notes: VAT (Law 4/2022) in force 1 Jan 2025 replacing IGV sales tax; 19% standard, 10% on certain essentials (basic foods, medicines).

GY.name: Guyana
GY.notes: 14% standard; many basic items zero-rated or exempt.

HK.name: Hong Kong
HK.notes: No VAT, GST or sales tax.

HN.name: Honduras
HN.notes: Sales tax (ISV) 15%; 18% on alcohol, tobacco and first/executive-class air tickets. Basic foods, medicines exempt.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.notes: 5% applies to listed basic foods (bread, milk, edible oils, baby food, fresh meat/fish, eggs, fruit, vegetables); other foods 13% or 25%. Daily newspapers of media publishers 5%, other periodicals 13%. Cinema/concert tickets 5%.

HT.name: Haiti
HT.notes: Turnover tax (TCA) 10% on goods and services per aggregator sources; not confirmed against DGI.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.notes: 5% on basic foods (meat, milk, eggs, bread etc.); some dairy/bakery 18%; other food 27%. Daily newspapers 0%, other periodicals 5%. Restaurant 5% covers food and non-alcoholic drinks prepared on site. Open-air festival tickets 18%.

ID.name: Indonesia
ID.notes: Local name PPN. Statutory rate 12% from 1 Jan 2025, but under PMK-131/2024 non-luxury goods/services are taxed at 12% on a deemed base of 11/12 of price, so the effective general rate is 11% (recorded here as standard). Luxury goods (also subject to PPnBM) pay the full 12% on full price. Officials said no VAT policy change for 2026; PwC (June 2026) still shows 12% statutory with 11% effective. Basic staples (rice, grains, eggs, vegetables, fresh meat/fish etc.) and public transport, medical and education services are VAT-exempt/not collected. Restaurants and hotels pay regional tax PBJT (max 10%) instead of VAT. Exports zero-rated.

IE.name: Ireland
IE.notes: Restaurant/catering food and hairdressing 13.5%->9% from 1 Jul 2026 (Budget 2026); hotel accommodation stays 13.5%. Gas and electricity 9% extended to 31 Dec 2030. Oral medicines 0%. Children's clothing/footwear (under 11) 0%. Passenger transport exempt. 4.8% livestock.

IL.name: Israel
IL.notes: Raised from 17% to 18% on 1 Jan 2025. Fresh fruits and vegetables zero-rated; Eilat free-trade zone has no VAT on local supplies. Exports zero-rated.

IM.name: Isle of Man
IM.notes: Single VAT territory with the UK; rules broadly identical to UK VAT (see GB). 5% on domestic property repairs and others.

IN.name: India
IN.notes: GST 2.0 from 22 Sep 2025 (56th GST Council): main slabs 5% (merit) and 18% (standard); 40% demerit rate for sin/luxury goods (pan masala, tobacco, aerated/sugary drinks, large cars/SUVs, yachts, private aircraft, betting/casinos/online gaming). 12% and 28% slabs abolished (most 12% items -> 5%, most 28% items -> 18%). Special rates kept: 3% gold/silver/jewellery, 0.25% rough/cut precious stones; nil for exempt goods. Compensation cess ended 1 Feb 2026 for tobacco (replaced by central excise + Health Security cess on pan masala; cigarettes/tobacco moved to 40% GST, bidi 18%). 57th Council (8 Oct 2026) kept rates unchanged. Category notes: food 0 = unpacked staples, milk, paneer, Indian breads (packaged foods mostly 5%); restaurant 5% without ITC (18% in hotels with room tariff > INR 7,500); books/newspapers/exercise books nil; medicines mostly 5% (33 life-saving drugs nil); apparel/footwear up to INR 2,500 5%, above 18%; road/rail/economy air passenger 5% (non-economy air 18%); hotel rooms up to INR 7,500/night 5%, above 18%; non-packaged water nil (packaged water 20L 5%, other bottled 18%); electricity is outside GST (state electricity duty instead); cinema tickets up to INR 100 5%, above INR 100 18%; entry to sporting events like IPL 40%. Petrol, diesel, ATF, natural gas, alcohol for human consumption are outside GST.
IN.split_note: Intra-state supply: CGST + SGST/UTGST, each half the rate (e.g. 18% = 9% CGST + 9% SGST). Inter-state supply and imports: IGST at the full rate.

IQ.name: Iraq
IQ.notes: No general VAT. Selective sales tax: 300% alcohol and tobacco, 15% travel tickets, 15% cars, 20% mobile recharge cards and internet, 10% deluxe/first-class restaurants and hotels.

IR.name: Iran
IR.notes: Raised from 9% to 10% from start of 1403 (20 Mar 2024). Proposed rise to 12% in the 1405 budget was rejected; rate remains 10%.

IS.name: Iceland
IS.notes: Local: VSK. 11% food, restaurant meals/catering, accommodation, books (incl. electronic), newspapers/magazines, radio/TV subscriptions, music, geothermal hot water/electricity/oil for space heating, travel agency/guiding services. Public transport, cultural and sports activities, healthcare exempt. Medicines at 24% (not in reduced list).

IT.name: Italy
IT.notes: 4% on basic foods (bread, milk, fresh fruit/vegetables, pasta, olive oil); many other foods 10%. Household electricity 10%. Livigno and Campione d'Italia are outside the VAT area.

JE.name: Jersey
JE.notes: Goods and Services Tax 5%, single rate; exports zero-rated; financial, medical, postal etc. exempt.

JM.name: Jamaica
JM.notes: GCT 15%; 10% on specified tourism activities. Basic foods and certain items zero-rated/exempt. Telecom services carry higher rate (25%).

JO.name: Jordan
JO.notes: General sales tax 16%. Reduced rates (e.g. 4%/5%/10%/2%) apply to listed goods; bread, tea, sugar, small packaged water and electricity exempt. Tourist restaurants pay 50% of rate (8%).

JP.name: Japan
JP.notes: 10% general (7.8% national + 2.2% local); 8% reduced for food and non-alcoholic beverages (not eating in restaurants, not alcohol) and newspaper subscriptions issued 2+ times weekly. Takeaway food 8%, dine-in 10%. Exports zero-rated; land, securities, medical care under public insurance, etc. not taxable. PENDING: bill to cut food rate 8%->1% for two years from April 2027 passed the lower house on 6 Nov 2026; not yet enacted (upper house pending).

KE.name: Kenya
KE.notes: 16% standard. Selected petroleum products (petrol, diesel, kerosene) temporarily 8% since 15 Apr 2026, extended to 14 Oct 2026 and again by Tax Laws (Amendment) Act 2026 (90-day extension). Ordinary bread, maize/wheat flour, milk zero-rated; unprocessed staples exempt.

KG.name: Kyrgyzstan
KG.notes: Local: NDS/KNS. 12% VAT (incl. imports, digital services) plus a separate sales tax (roughly 1-5% depending on activity/payment).

KH.name: Cambodia
KH.notes: 10% VAT. Exempt: public postal services, medical/dental services, electricity, water, passenger transport by wholly state-owned public transport, insurance, primary financial services, land. Exports zero-rated.

KI.name: Kiribati
KI.notes: VAT 12.5%; VAT (Amendment) Act 2025 (from 1 Jan 2026) adds non-resident digital services, no rate change.

KM.name: Comoros
KM.notes: Consumption tax 10% standard, with special 0/3/5/7.5/25% cases (art. 152).

KN.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
KN.notes: 17% standard (temporarily 13% from 1 Jan to 30 Jun 2025, back to 17% from 1 Jul 2025). 10% on hotel accommodation and restaurant services (aggregator sources). Government declares occasional discounted-VAT days.

KP.name: North Korea
KP.notes: No VAT/GST on consumers (state economy; no published consumption tax).

KR.name: South Korea
KR.notes: Single 10% rate. Exempt: unprocessed foods and agricultural products, tap water, medical and health services, education, books/newspapers/magazines (excluding advertising), mass passenger transport (not air, express/chartered buses, taxis, high-speed rail), finance and insurance. Exports and international transport zero-rated.

KW.name: Kuwait
KW.notes: No VAT. GCC framework under discussion; 2026-2030 fiscal plan makes no provision for VAT.

KY.name: Cayman Islands
KY.notes: No VAT or sales tax; import duty and tourism accommodation tax apply (PwC: VAT NA).

KZ.name: Kazakhstan
KZ.notes: Local: NDS/QQS. New Tax Code (No. 214-VIII) from 1 Jan 2026: standard 12 -> 16%. 5% (10% from 2027) on listed medicines, medical devices and medical services. 10% on domestic periodicals. 0% exports.

LA.name: Laos
LA.notes: VAT cut 10%->7% from 1 Jan 2022, reinstated to 10% by Ordinance 003/POL (19 Mar 2024), applied from 1 May 2024 (MOF Notice 1360). Exempt: unprocessed agricultural products, educational goods/services, certain medical goods/services, financial services.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.notes: Standard 11%. Exports and international transport zero-rated; banking, financial and insurance exempt.

LC.name: Saint Lucia
LC.notes: 12.5% standard (since 1 Dec 2020); 10% other tourism services; 7% hotel accommodation.

LI.name: Liechtenstein
LI.notes: Applies Swiss VAT law with its own administration; rates identical to Switzerland (7.7/2.5/3.7 until 31 Dec 2023).

LK.name: Sri Lanka
LK.notes: VAT raised 15%->18% from 1 Jan 2024 (and many exemptions removed). Financial services VAT 20.5% from 1 Jul 2026 (VAT (Amendment) Act No. 14 of 2026). Finance Ministry confirmed 18% general rate unchanged in 2026. A separate 2.5% Social Security Contribution Levy (SSCL) on turnover still applies to most businesses and is often passed on in prices. Some supplies exempt; exports zero-rated.

LR.name: Liberia
LR.notes: GST 13% (raised from 12% on 1 May 2026, Tax Amendment Act 2026); telecom 15%; exports 0%. VAT at 15% replaces GST from 1 Jan 2027.

LT.name: Lithuania
LT.notes: From 1 Jan 2026: the 9% rate became 12% (accommodation, scheduled domestic passenger transport, cultural events); books 9%->5%; district heating 9%->21%. Medicines 5% only when reimbursed (others 21%).

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.notes: Temporary 2023 cut (16/13/7) ended 31 Dec 2023; 17/14/8/3 again from 1 Jan 2024. Restaurant 3% excludes alcohol (17%). Children's clothing/footwear (up to 13) 3%. Domestic public transport is free of charge.

LV.name: Latvia
LV.notes: 12% pilot for bread, milk, fresh poultry and eggs from 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027; locally typical fresh fruit, berries and vegetables 12% (made permanent from 1 Jan 2026); baby food 12%; other food 21%.

LY.name: Libya
LY.notes: No VAT/sales tax; 5% service fee on most imports.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.notes: 2024 Finance Act reform completed in 2026: only 20% and 10% (7% and 14% abolished). Domestic water and pharmaceuticals exempt with deduction (0%); milk, bread, cereals, sugar(raw), newspapers, books exempt; conventional electricity now 20%, renewable 10%; urban/road transport 10%.

MC.name: Monaco
MC.notes: Monaco applies French VAT (1963 Franco-Monegasque convention); all rates and categories identical to France (see FR entry).

MD.name: Moldova
MD.notes: Local: TVA. 8% bread and bakery, milk and dairy, natural gas, HoReCa (hotels, restaurants, cafes). HoReCa was temporarily 6% 16 Dec 2024 - 13 Feb 2025 (energy emergency), back to 8% from 14 Feb 2025. Government 2027 bill to raise HoReCa to 12% pending, not enacted.

ME.name: Montenegro
ME.notes: Local: PDV. New 15% rate from 1 Jan 2025: books, accommodation, food & beverage service in hospitality (excl. alcohol, sugared drinks, coffee), entry tickets. 7%: basic food, medicines, drinking water (not bottled), newspapers, textbooks, public transport, menstrual products, baby diapers.

MF.name: Saint Martin
MF.notes: French VAT does not apply; local general turnover tax (TGCA) 4%.

MH.name: Marshall Islands
MH.notes: No national VAT/GST/sales tax; gross revenue tax on businesses; local governments (Majuro, Kwajalein) levy local sales taxes. IMF (2025) recommends a 10% VAT; not adopted.

MK.name: North Macedonia
MK.notes: Local: DDV. 5% food, drinking water, medicines, books/newspapers, household electricity, passenger transport, accommodation, baby products, school supplies. 10% restaurant/catering (excl. alcohol). Fuel temporarily 10% (from Mar 2026, extended to ~Sep/Oct 2026).

MM.name: Myanmar
MM.notes: No VAT. Commercial tax (turnover-style with input credits) at 0-15%; general rate 5% on most goods and services; 3% hotel and tourism services; 1% gold/jewellery; 15% internet services; 47 goods and 34 services exempt.

MN.name: Mongolia
MN.notes: 10% VAT on goods, services and works; exports zero-rated; registration threshold MNT 50 million.

MO.name: Macao
MO.notes: No VAT; only consumption tax on tobacco and spirits.

MQ.name: Martinique
MQ.notes: French overseas department: 8.5% normal rate, 2.1% reduced rate.

MS.name: Montserrat
MS.notes: No broad VAT; consumption tax on imports under commodity schedules.

MT.name: Malta
MT.notes: Food for home consumption and pharmaceuticals 0% (exempt with credit); confectionery 5%. Licensed accommodation 7%. Scheduled public transport and public water supply exempt.

MU.name: Mauritius
MU.notes: 15%; zero-rated basic foodstuffs (rice, flour, bread, edible oil, milk etc.); e-books zero-rated by Finance Act 2026 (13 Aug 2026).

MV.name: Maldives
MV.notes: General GST 8% (since 1 Jan 2023). Tourism GST (T-GST) 17% from 1 Jul 2025 (was 16%) on resorts, hotels, guesthouses, tourist vessels and tourism services; extended to offshore tourism/booking suppliers from 1 Oct 2026 (8th amendment). Some basic goods and services zero-rated/exempt.

MW.name: Malawi
MW.notes: Raised from 16.5% to 17.5% by Value Added (Amendment) Act 2025, gazetted 30 Dec 2025, in force 31 Dec 2025.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.notes: 16% general. 8% effective rate in the northern (and southern) border region via a 50% IVA credit for registered businesses; decree extended to 31 Dec 2026 (DOF 31 Dec 2025). 0%: basic unprocessed foodstuffs, medicines, books/newspapers/magazines published by the taxpayer, domestic-use water, exports, agricultural goods. Prepared food/restaurants 16%. Exempt: medical services, education, residential rent, land public transport of persons (not 0-rated legally, but no IVA charged).

MY.name: Malaysia
MY.notes: No VAT/GST since 2018; two single-stage taxes. Sales tax (goods): 10% standard, 5% reduced, many basic foods exempt; scope widened 1 Jul 2025 (e.g. imported premium fish/fruits, some construction materials now 5%/10%). Service tax (services): 8% general since 1 Mar 2024; 6% for F&B, telecoms, parking, logistics, construction, private healthcare and education; rental/leasing cut 8%->6% from 1 Jan 2026 (MSME threshold RM1.5m). 'standard' = sales tax 10%; 'service_tax' = 8%. Restaurant 6% applies only to outlets above the service-tax threshold; hotel accommodation 8%.

MZ.name: Mozambique
MZ.notes: 16% (cut from 17% in 2023); 5% on selected supplies; certain basic foodstuffs zero-rated.

NC.name: New Caledonia
NC.notes: Taxe generale sur la consommation: normal 11%, reduced 3%, specific 6%, higher 22% (luxury/alcohol/tobacco etc.).

NF.name: Norfolk Island
NF.notes: Australian GST applies since 1 Jul 2016 (same rules as Australia).

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.notes: 7.5% since 1 Feb 2020; retained by Nigeria Tax Act 2025 (in force 1 Jan 2026). Zero-rated: basic food items, medical and pharmaceutical products, educational books and materials, exports, some electricity generation/transmission.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.notes: Hotel/overnight accommodation 9%->21% from 1 Jan 2026 (camping pitches stay 9%). Planned 2026 rise for culture, media and sport was reversed (stays 9%). Caribbean Netherlands (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, Saba) use ABB, not VAT.

NO.name: Norway
NO.notes: Local name MVA (merverdiavgift). 15% food & drink (not served in restaurants; not tobacco/alcohol/medicines) and, from 1 Jul 2025, water & wastewater. 12% passenger transport, accommodation, cinema, museums, amusement parks, sports events (theatre/concerts generally exempt). Books, newspapers, e-books/e-news zero-rated. 11.11% special rate for wild marine resources sold by fishers. Electric cars zero-rated only up to NOK 300,000 from 1 Jan 2026 (was 500,000). Electricity for households in Nord-Norge exempt.

NP.name: Nepal
NP.notes: Single 13% rate until FY 2082/83. Budget 2083/84 (29 May 2026) introduced a multi-rate system 0%/5%/13% from mid-July 2026 (Shrawan 2083): 5% on household electricity and ride-sharing services; 13% unchanged for everything else. Basic food, health, education services exempt.

NR.name: Nauru
NR.notes: No VAT/GST or general consumption tax (VAT under discussion only).

NU.name: Niue
NU.notes: Niue Consumption Tax (NCT) 12.5% since 1 Apr 2009 (modelled on NZ GST); medical services and exports exempt/zero.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.notes: Single 15% rate with very few exemptions (financial services, residential rent). No reduced rate for food. 0% only for exports, some land and going-concern sales.

OM.name: Oman
OM.notes: VAT introduced 16 Apr 2021. 0% on listed basic food items, exports, international transport; local passenger transport, education, residential rent, some financial services exempt.

PA.name: Panama
PA.notes: ITBMS 7% general; higher rates 10% (alcoholic beverages, hotel/lodging) and 15% (tobacco products). Many foods and medicines exempt.

PE.name: Peru
PE.notes: 18% = 16% IGV + 2% Municipal Promotion Tax (IPM). Micro and small businesses whose main activity is restaurants, hotels, tourist accommodation, catering or food concessions: 8% IGV + 2% IPM = 10% for 2025-2026 (Law 31556 as extended by Law 32219); 12% IGV (+2% IPM = 14%) in 2027; 18% from 2028. Larger restaurants/hotels charge 18%. Many unprocessed basic foods and some other items are exempt (Appendix I/II). Exports not subject to IGV.

PF.name: French Polynesia
PF.notes: TVA: 16% normal (goods), 13% services, reduced rate for some items (commonly cited 5%; not confirmed from official page). From 1 Jul 2026 a 1% rate applies to eligible supplies in the remote archipelagos outside the Society Islands.

PG.name: Papua New Guinea
PG.notes: 10% GST; exports zero-rated; medical, educational and financial services exempt.

PH.name: Philippines
PH.notes: Uniform 12% VAT. Exempt: unprocessed agricultural/food products in original state, books, newspapers and magazines, specified medicines (diabetes, cholesterol, hypertension, cancer, mental illness, TB, kidney disease), plus many services. Exports zero-rated. VAT on digital services by non-residents from 2 Jun 2025 (RA 12023).

PK.name: Pakistan
PK.notes: Federal sales tax on goods 18% (raised from 17% in Feb 2023); some goods at reduced/specific rates or exempt (Sixth/Eighth Schedules); exports zero-rated; 3% value-addition tax on commercial imports. Services are taxed by provinces: Punjab 16%; Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and Islamabad (ICT) 15% (PwC: 15-16% range), with reduced rates for some services (e.g. restaurants paid by card in some provinces).

PL.name: Poland
PL.notes: Basic food 5% (0% ended 31 Mar 2024); some food 8%. Restaurant 8% (coffee, tea, soft drinks, alcohol 23%). Motor fuel temporarily 8% in 2026 windows (latest 3 Oct-31 Dec 2026).

PR.name: Puerto Rico
PR.notes: Sales and use tax 11.5% (10.5% state + 1% municipal) on tangible personal property and certain services; 4% on business-to-business and designated professional services. Unprocessed food, prescription medicines exempt. US territory (not in the US 'states' table).

PS.name: Palestine
PS.notes: VAT 16% on taxable deals and imports.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.notes: Some foods 13% or 23%. Restaurant 13% excludes alcohol and soft drinks. 6% on the fixed part of small (<=3.45 kVA) electricity contracts. Azores 16% and Madeira 22% standard.

PW.name: Palau
PW.notes: Palau Goods and Services Tax (PGST) 10% from 1 Jan 2023 (modelled on Australian GST), replacing gross revenue tax.

PY.name: Paraguay
PY.notes: 10% general; 5% on sale/rent of real estate, some medicines, and agricultural/horticultural/fruit products and basic-basket items.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.notes: No VAT or sales tax. GCC VAT (expected 5%) not yet introduced; no legislation in force as of Nov 2026.

RE.name: Réunion
RE.notes: French overseas department with its own TVA rates (same in Guadeloupe and Martinique): 8.5% normal, 2.1% reduced, 1.05% press; some essential goods and air/sea transport 0%.

RO.name: Romania
RO.notes: From 1 Aug 2025: standard 19%->21%; the 5% and 9% rates merged into one 11% rate. Foods with high added sugar are excluded from 11%. Restaurant 11% excludes alcohol.

RS.name: Serbia
RS.notes: Local: PDV. 10% basic food, daily newspapers, medicines, publications/textbooks, public transport, accommodation, some utilities (gas, district heating). Restaurant service 20%.

RU.name: Russia
RU.notes: Local: NDS. 10% on government lists of basic foodstuffs, children's goods, periodicals and educational/scientific/cultural books (non-advertising), medical goods (many registered medicines are exempt). 0% hotel/temporary accommodation (registered facilities) extended to 31 Dec 2030 by Law 227-FZ of 23 Jul 2025. Simplified-regime (USN) sellers may charge special 5% or 7% VAT since 1 Jan 2025. Urban public passenger transport generally exempt.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.notes: 18%; exports 0%; clean water and other supplies exempt.

SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.notes: Raised from 5% on 1 July 2020. Qualifying medicines and medical equipment (MoH/SFDA list) zero-rated; private healthcare/education standard-rated (state bears VAT for citizens). Food is standard-rated.

SB.name: Solomon Islands
SB.notes: No VAT yet. VAT Bill 2025 proposes a single 15% VAT replacing goods tax, sales tax, stamp duty and accommodation levy; implementation now reported for 2028. Current sales tax on goods/services commonly cited at 10% (goods tax on imports up to 15%) - secondary sources only.

SD.name: Sudan
SD.notes: 17% general (secondary sources); higher rates on telecoms. Staple food imports exempted Oct 2026.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.notes: Food temporarily 12%->6% from 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Dec 2027 (takeaway food 6%; eating in 12%). Tap water standard rate. Prescription medicines 0%.

SG.name: Singapore
SG.notes: GST 8%->9% from 1 Jan 2024. No reduced rates: only exemptions for prescribed financial services, sale/rental of residential property, digital payment tokens and investment precious metals; zero-rating for exports and international services. Food, books, medicine, transport, hotels all at 9%.

SK.name: Slovakia
SK.notes: From 1 Jan 2025: standard 20%->23%, 10% replaced by 19% and 5%. Selected basic foods (meat, fish, milk, butter, bread, etc.) 5%; other food 19% (high-sugar/salt foods 23% from 2026). Restaurant food 5%, non-alcoholic drinks 19%.

SL.name: Sierra Leone
SL.notes: GST 15%; Finance Act 2026 revised zero-rated schedule and taxes non-resident digital services from 1 Jan 2026.

SM.name: San Marino
SM.notes: No VAT. Imposta monofase (single-stage tax) of 17% levied once on imported goods (Delegated Decree 183/2011); lower rates for certain goods (e.g. food reportedly 2%, cars 7%) unverified. Retail prices normally include it; not charged at checkout like VAT.

SO.name: Somalia
SO.notes: Federal sales tax 5% (direct collection from businesses from Aug 2024); formal VAT under development.

SR.name: Suriname
SR.notes: VAT (BTW) introduced 1 Jan 2023 replacing turnover tax: 10% standard; a 25% rate on certain luxury goods; 5% and 0% rates per the VAT Act (detail lists unconfirmed from official text).

SS.name: South Sudan
SS.notes: Sales tax 18% (20% on hotel/restaurant/bar per 2023/24 Financial Act). VAT law still in draft as of mid-2026.

ST.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
ST.notes: VAT in force 1 Jun 2023; 7.5% on basket of basic foods (rice, flour etc.).

SX.name: Sint Maarten
SX.notes: Turnover tax 5% on gross business revenues, typically passed on. Currency: Caribbean guilder (XCG) since 31 Mar 2025.

TC.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
TC.notes: No VAT or general sales tax; customs duty and hotel & restaurant tax apply.

TD.name: Chad
TD.notes: 18%; 9% on certain local products (cement, sugar, oil, soap, textiles); 0% exports and local agri-food products.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.notes: Statutory rate 10%, reduced to 7% by royal decree; the 7% rate is extended to 30 Sep 2027 (Royal Decree 807). Exempt: unprocessed agricultural products, newspapers/magazines/textbooks, domestic land transport, medical and educational services. Exports zero-rated. Hotels and restaurants charge 7% VAT (service charges common).

TJ.name: Tajikistan
TJ.notes: Local: AAI. Tax Code 2022 Art. 397(4): 14% from 1 Jan 2024 to 31 Dec 2026, 13% from 1 Jan 2027 (Art. 264 statutory 15%). 7% construction, hotel and catering; 5% domestic agricultural products, training, sanatorium services.

TL.name: Timor-Leste
TL.notes: No VAT yet. Sales tax 2.5% on imports and on certain domestic supplies (hotel, restaurant/bar, telecom services above threshold). VAT planned for 2027 (rate not announced).

TM.name: Turkmenistan
TM.notes: Local: GBS. 15% standard (Tax Code Art. 103); 0% exports (Art. 105); exemptions Art. 106.

TN.name: Tunisia
TN.notes: 19% / 13% / 7% since 1 Jan 2018. 2025 Finance Law: new housing 13% replaced by 7% (≤ TND 400k) or 19%.

TO.name: Tonga
TO.notes: Consumption Tax (CT) 15% on most goods and services; no change found for 2025-2026.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.notes: Standard 18→20% and reduced 8→10% on 10 July 2023 (Decree 7346); 1% unchanged. List I (1%): certain agricultural products, some basic foods, financial leasing. List II (10%): basic foodstuffs, textiles, books and similar publications. Exact food rate depends on product (1% or 10%).

TT.name: Trinidad and Tobago
TT.notes: 12.5% standard; basic foods, medicines and others zero-rated.

TV.name: Tuvalu
TV.notes: Consumption Tax Act (2008); rate 7% per IMF 2022 Pacific tax paper. Sources conflict (some aggregators list 0%, 5% or 20%); low confidence.

TW.name: Taiwan
TW.notes: Business tax: 5% VAT for general industries; gross business receipts tax (GBRT) 1-5% for financial institutions and small businesses instead of VAT. Exports zero-rated; unprocessed agricultural products and some basic items exempt.

TZ.name: Tanzania
TZ.notes: Mainland 18%; 16% for specified B2C purchases paid electronically (Finance Act 2025, on hold pending notice). Zanzibar: 15% general, 18% banking/postal/telecom.

UA.name: Ukraine
UA.notes: Local: PDV. 14% certain agricultural products (corn, soybeans, sunflower seeds etc.). 7% qualifying medicines and medical goods, temporary accommodation, museum/zoo/reserve visits and other cultural events, tickets to sports events. 0% exports/international transport. Proposals (5% essentials, 21% standard for 2027) NOT enacted as of Nov 2026; parcel-VAT law 5025-IX takes effect 1 Jul 2027.

US.name: United States
US.notes: No federal sales tax/VAT; state + local sales taxes apply. 'states' = Tax Foundation table as of 1 Jul 2026 (no statewide base-rate changes Jan-Jul 2026); avg_local is population-weighted. CA, UT, VA mandatory statewide local add-ons (1.25/1.25/1%) are included in state_rate. NJ avg_local is negative because Salem County collects 3.3125% instead of the state rate. Groceries: most states exempt food at state level (state rate cuts: KS 0% from 1 Jan 2025, OK 0% from 29 Aug 2024, IL state 1% repealed 1 Jan 2026 (local option), AR 0.125% repealed 1 Jan 2026, MS 7%->5% 1 Jul 2025). DC general rate 6% until 30 Sep 2027, scheduled 7% from 1 Oct 2027 (OTR).

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.notes: 22% basic; 10% minimum rate on certain goods/services (e.g. basic foods, medicines, hotel services). Exports zero-rated.

UZ.name: Uzbekistan
UZ.notes: Local: QQS. 12% standard. From 1 Jan 2026 farmers' own agricultural produce (excl. grain, cotton) at 0%. Optional 6% simplified VAT regime for small catering/trade/service businesses from 1 Jun 2026.

VC.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
VC.notes: 16% standard; 11% on hotel accommodation; zero-rated basic items.

VE.name: Venezuela
VE.notes: 16% general; 8% reduced on certain items; additional 15% on luxury goods (31% total). Separate 3% tax on large financial transactions (IGTF) on payments in foreign currency.

VG.name: British Virgin Islands
VG.notes: No VAT or general sales tax; customs duty and hotel accommodation tax apply.

VI.name: US Virgin Islands
VI.notes: No sales tax; businesses pay a gross receipts tax (not itemised to consumers).

VN.name: Vietnam
VN.notes: Statutory standard 10%. Temporary 2-point cut to 8% for most goods/services otherwise at 10% (excludes telecoms, banking/finance, real estate, metals, mining, coke/petroleum, SCT goods) from 1 Jul 2025 to 31 Dec 2026 (Resolution 204/2025/QH15, Decree 174/2025/ND-CP); before that the 8% cut ran in successive 6-month periods since 2022. New VAT Law 48/2024/QH15 in force 1 Jul 2025. 5% rate: clean water, medicines and medical equipment, teaching aids, unprocessed farm products at commercial stage, books (other than textbooks/political books), children's toys, traditional performing arts. Non-taxable: newspapers/textbooks, bus/tram/waterway mass transit, medical services. Exports 0%.

VU.name: Vanuatu
VU.notes: VAT 15% on most goods and services (raised from 12.5% earlier); exports zero-rated.

WS.name: Samoa
WS.notes: Value Added Goods and Services Tax 15% (unchanged 2025-2026 per secondary sources); exports zero-rated.

YE.name: Yemen
YE.notes: General sales tax 5% (Law 19 of 2001); 10% on some telecom services; essentials exempt. System operates in limited capacity due to conflict.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.notes: Only 15% and 0%. Proposed increase to 15.5%/16% (2025 budget) withdrawn; 2026 budget kept 15%. Zero-rated basic foodstuffs (e.g. brown bread, maize meal, rice, fresh fruit and vegetables, milk, eggs). Non-international passenger road/rail transport, residential rent, education exempt.

ZW.name: Zimbabwe
ZW.notes: Raised from 15% to 15.5% on 1 Jan 2026 (Finance Act No.7 of 2025, s.34). Medicines and agricultural goods moved from zero-rated to exempt (still no VAT to consumer).
